candidate.answerReason: The only admissible dimension pairs are (5,12) and (6,8), so there are two possibilities.

methods.label: Turn the area equation into factor pairs
methods.explanation:
A border of width \(1\) removes \(2\) feet from each painted dimension. Thus \(a>2\), \(b>2\), and the painted rectangle has dimensions \(a-2\) and \(b-2\). Since the border occupies half the floor, the painted rectangle also occupies half:
\[
(a-2)(b-2)=\frac{ab}{2}.
\]
Expanding and rearranging gives
\[
ab-4a-4b+8=0,
\]
so adding \(8\) to both sides completes a product:
\[
(a-4)(b-4)=8.
\]
We must determine the signs before listing factors. The expanded equation also gives \(b(a-4)=4(a-2)>0\). Since \(b>0\), we have \(a>4\), and hence \(b>4\).

Therefore \(a-4\) and \(b-4\) are positive integers whose product is \(8\). Because \(b>a\), the first factor must be smaller. The complete list is
\[
(a-4,b-4)=(1,8),\ (2,4),
\]
giving \((a,b)=(5,12)\) and \((6,8)\). Their painted areas are respectively \(3\cdot10=30\), half of \(60\), and \(4\cdot6=24\), half of \(48\). Both satisfy all conditions. Reversing either pair would violate \(b>a\), so there are exactly \(\boxed{2}\) possibilities, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Factoring a school-algebra equation and listing the factor pairs of 8 are within AMC 12 scope.

methods.label: Restrict the shorter side first
methods.explanation:
The painted fraction of the floor is
\[
\frac{(a-2)(b-2)}{ab}
=\left(1-\frac2a\right)\left(1-\frac2b\right)
=\frac12,
\]
where \(b>a>2\). This product lets us restrict \(a\) before solving for \(b\).

If \(a\le4\), the first factor is at most \(1/2\), while the second factor is positive and less than \(1\). Their product would be less than \(1/2\), which is impossible.

If \(a\ge7\), integrality and \(b>a\) give \(b\ge8\). Then
\[
\left(1-\frac2a\right)\left(1-\frac2b\right)
\ge\frac57\cdot\frac34
=\frac{15}{28}>\frac12,
\]
which is also impossible. Hence the only possible shorter sides are \(a=5\) and \(a=6\).

For \(a=5\), the area equation becomes
\[
3(b-2)=\frac{5b}{2},
\]
so \(6b-12=5b\) and \(b=12\). For \(a=6\), it becomes \(4(b-2)=3b\), giving \(b=8\).

Both pairs have positive painted dimensions and satisfy \(b>a\) and the half-area condition. The bounds exclude every other value of \(a\), and each remaining value gives exactly one \(b\). Thus there are \(\boxed{2}\) possibilities, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).

candidate.annotationRationale: The task asks for all integer solutions satisfying geometric restrictions, so integer-equation solving is the route-neutral target. Rectangle area supports both methods. Polynomial expansion and factor pairs belong to the first route; integer bounds, inequality comparisons, and linear equations belong to the second. Neither alternative is a requirement of the other.

review.mathematicalCheck: The painted-area condition gives (a-4)(b-4)=8. The sign argument establishes a>4, leaving precisely the ordered factor pairs (1,8) and (2,4), hence dimensions (5,12) and (6,8). Independently, the fraction bounds exclude a≤4 and a≥7, and solving the two remaining cases yields the same complete list.
